 Florida food bank turns people away as demand stays high months after 12-day SNAP pause
 "A lot of these people are working two and three jobs and still can't make it."
 by Kim LaCapria November 2, 2026 
 share
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Link Copied! 
 Photo Credit: Hope Village of America
 A food bank in Clearwater, Florida, is struggling to keep its shelves stocked nearly a year after a disruption to federal food assistance sent hundreds of households looking for help.
 The shortage forced Hope Villages of America to turn people away in the months following what started as a 12-day interruption, Bay News 9 reported.
 Here's what to know
 Hope Villages of America still assists more than 150 households daily. 
 Before Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits paused amid a November 2025 federal shutdown, the organization typically assisted roughly 120-140 households each day.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hope Villages of America (@hopevillages) 
 The warehouse's food reserves were quickly depleted as more families sought help during the interruption.
 "When the benefits paused, we had an overnight spike in our numbers, where we were serving over 200 to 300 households a day," recalled Lindsey Peek, Hope Villages of America's community engagement director.

 Benefits have since resumed, although permanent cuts have slashed eligibility in Florida and nationwide.
 According to Peek, 1 in 10 Pinellas County residents depends on SNAP benefits to put food on their tables.
 More background
 Many residents do not earn enough to cover their food needs, according to Elizabeth Brown, a volunteer who checked visitors in at their vehicles.
 "Surprisingly, a lot of these people are working two and three jobs and still can't make it, which is really alarming," Brown told the station.
 The amount of food available at Hope Villages has fallen along with donations , though demand has stayed high.
 "People just aren't able to give like they used to," Peek said.
 What's being done?
 To keep assistance available to residents in need, Hope Villages of America welcomes food and monetary donations .
 Peek explained that the food bank operates for fewer hours and closes early because its supplies are running low.
 "We've had to decrease our volunteer capacity because we simply don't have jobs for people to do without food coming into the food bank," Peek said.
 The shelves for reserve supplies were bare at the Clearwater food bank. Peek showed Bay News 9 how shelves and bins lacked their usual pantry stocks.
 "An empty shelf means an empty table," she warned.
 Where can I learn more?
 Across Florida, food programs are struggling with rising demand and shrinking supplies. These stories cover rising grocery costs, pantry demand, and funding losses affecting food programs.
 • In Northwest Florida, weekly food pantry trips become routine as SNAP cuts and grocery prices bite.
 • In Port Richey, a Salvation Army pantry served 100 people in three hours , up from 30 daily.
 • In South Florida, 1.7 million people struggle to put food on the table as costs rise.
 • In Osceola County, Salvation Army mobile pantry demand jumped 68% as the organization seeks help.
